Air Quality Index: 0.5 (Good). The remnants of former Hurricane Rachel brought the heaviest rain to our area since former Hurricane Hillary back in August 2023. Some local flooding occurred but nothing major in our immediate location, mainly ponding of water in lower-lying spots but we’re at a higher elevation than most of the valley so likely more issues at the lower locations. Between 8:00 PM on 10/10/2026 and 6:30 AM today, 1.78” was measured (another 0.01” fell early afternoon yesterday) in the CoCoRaHS gauge. The recording gauge (Davis Vantage Pro2) measured 1.99” with a maximum rain rate of 3.84”/hour at 11:15 PM on the 10th. Our average annual precipitation for this location is 3.44" (PRISM model), 3.60" (NOAA model), making this event half of our annual average.

The October 9–11, 2026 Rachel weather event brought a period of heightened meteorological concern to Southern California, including  station A-OR-115 in central Yorba Linda. Forecast guidance initially indicated the potential for significant overnight rainfall, locally heavy precipitation bands, and gusty winds, with the greatest concern extending into Sunday morning, October 11. The anticipated rainfall window was subsequently revised as Rachel's associated weather system advanced northward faster than forecast, causing the primary rain and wind threat to diminish earlier than expected. By the morning of October 11, the remaining precipitation was becoming more scattered, with isolated showers still possible later in the day.
